note.text: A letter’s relationship and purpose affect its tone. A formal school request uses respectful clear wording, a suitable salutation, organised content and an appropriate close. An informal letter to a friend can sound more personal while remaining clear. Include the addresses, date and other elements the task and examination convention require; exact layouts may vary. Do not treat contractions as universally forbidden or friendliness as an excuse for missing the purpose. Use fictional addresses in classroom practice.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to write a letter whose layout, tone and content fit its reader and purpose. Builds on: directed-writing instructions and paragraph planning. Leads to: talks, reports and controlled changes of register.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: Formal miniature: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing on behalf of our fictional reading club to request permission to use the library after lessons. We propose supervised discussion and careful return of materials. Please let us know the arrangements required. Yours faithfully, Bih. Informal miniature: Dear Ayuk, Our club is planning a reading afternoon. I hope you can join us and bring a story suggestion. Write and tell me what you think. Best wishes, Bih.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Plan the request or message before adding the conventional frame. Match salutation and close, give the reason and state the response wanted. For the paper task, add fictitious address/date details in the teacher’s preferred layout. Compare tone without inventing one universal layout for every context.

Informal miniature: Dear Ayuk, Our club is planning a reading afternoon. I hope you can join us and bring a story suggestion. Write and tell me what you think. Best wishes, Bih.
